A full traverse avoids reversing technical terrain but makes for a long day.

days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp in Boston Basin
days.note: Hike the climbers' path from the trailhead into Boston Basin and camp near 6,400 ft below the peak.

days.title: West Ridge to summit, descend couloir
days.objective: Climb the West Ridge and return to camp
days.note: Pre-dawn start up the approach couloir to the West Ridge notch, then ~6 pitches of low 5th-class ridge climbing to the true summit. Reverse the ridge to the notch and descend the couloir back to camp, hiking out the same evening or the next morning.

camps_on_file.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps_on_file.notes: The standard base for the route, in the boulder-and-heather basin below the south face, roughly 3 miles and 3,000 ft above the trailhead. Most parties leave camp very early and are back the same day; it is also the place to retreat to if the couloir or the ridge turns you around.

camps_on_file.name: Treeline emergency bivy
camps_on_file.notes: Not a planned camp and not a substitute for reaching the basin. An emergency option only: parties benighted on the walk in have stopped near treeline on the Boston Basin path; there are no prepared sites and no reason to aim for it.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip: hike in to Boston Basin, a long round-trip summit day on the South Ridge, and hike out — about 5,300 ft of gain over roughly 10 miles round trip.

days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp below Torment's South Ridge
days.note: A steep, rough climbers' trail off Cascade River Road gains about 3,000 ft in 3-4 hours to benched campsites in upper Boston Basin beneath the Taboo Glacier and Torment's South Ridge.

days.title: Climb the South Ridge, return to camp
days.objective: Summit Mount Torment via the South Ridge
days.note: An alpine start crosses the gentle Taboo Glacier to a snow couloir gaining the South Ridge; four pitches of low-5th-class rock lead to the summit, with the moat/bergschrund at the base often the crux in mid-to-late season. trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, 2-night trip (about 30 hours on the move): hike in, climb Torment and bivy on the connecting ridge, then finish over Forbidden and descend all the way to the car; strong parties sometimes do it all in one very long push.

days.title: Approach to Boston Basin camp
days.objective: Establish camp below the Taboo Glacier
days.note: A steep, rough climbers' trail off Cascade River Road gains about 3,000 ft in 3-4 hours to benched campsites in upper Boston Basin below the Taboo Glacier. Afternoon is spent racking up and scouting the couloir for the next day's alpine start.

days.title: Climb Torment, bivy on the connecting ridge
days.objective: Summit Mount Torment and reach a bivy site on the traverse ridge
days.note: An alpine start crosses the Taboo Glacier to a snow/rock couloir that gains Torment's south ridge; low-5th-class rock leads to the summit around midday. Rather than pushing straight on to Forbidden, most parties downclimb and traverse the connecting ridge and find a bivy ledge in the early evening.

days.title: Finish the traverse over Forbidden, descend to the car
days.objective: Summit Forbidden Peak and return to the trailhead
days.note: From the ridge bivy, parties reach the notch below Forbidden's West Ridge by mid-morning, simul-climb to the summit around noon, then descend via the West Ridge and the Cat Scratch Gullies (roughly 6-8 rappels) back to Boston Basin and out to the trailhead, often not reaching the car until evening.

camps_on_file.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps_on_file.notes: A comfortable planned camp, roughly 6,300 to 6,400 ft, on a small sandy flat at the foot of a permanent snowfield with a privy and a food storage bin nearby. camps_on_file.notes: A planned alternative camp for parties who want to start the traverse from the base of the climbing instead of from Boston Basin. camps_on_file.name: Mid-traverse ridge bivy
camps_on_file.notes: This is the emergency-and-committed option rather than a planned camp: a flat spot at a notch on the ridge roughly midway along the traverse, reached after the snow and ice section on the north side. trip_plan.totalNote: A classic 3-day glacier climb (2 nights in Boston Basin) totaling roughly 10.5 mi and 5,500 ft of gain; strong, fit rope teams commonly compress it into a 2-day trip by hiking out the same day they summit.

days.title: Approach to Boston Basin high camp
days.objective: Reach camp in Boston Basin below Sharkfin Tower
days.note: From the Boston Basin Trailhead off Cascade River Road, a steep, well-worn climbers' trail through timber and stream crossings gains the alpine basin. Camp around 6,200-6,700 ft with views of Sahale, Sharkfin, and Boston Peak.

days.title: Quien Sabe Glacier summit day
days.objective: Climb Sahale Peak via the Quien Sabe Glacier and return to camp
days.note: A pre-dawn alpine start to rope up on the glacier, climb to the Boston-Sahale col, then traverse an exposed class 3-4 ridge to the summit. Round trip from camp typically runs 7-9 hours for a fit, efficient rope team.

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Boston Basin trailhead
days.note: Break camp after breakfast and descend the same trail back to the car; strong parties often skip this night and combine the summit push with the hike out on day 2 instead.

camps_on_file.name: Boston Basin high camp
camps_on_file.notes: The upper of the basin's two camps, around 6,400 ft, with a composting toilet. It is the natural base for the Quien Sabe: the glacier starts more or less at the tent door, so summit day is short. Snow lingers here well into July, and the rule to pitch only on hardened ground matters — the meadows recover very slowly.

camps_on_file.name: Boston Basin low camp
camps_on_file.notes: Around 5,300 ft on the edge of a moraine crest among small trees, below the polished slabs the Quien Sabe has left behind. Melts out earlier and is more sheltered than the high camp, at the cost of an extra thousand feet on summit morning.

trip_plan.totalNote: A popular 1-night backpack: ~13 mi round trip and ~5,000 ft gain, with an alpine-start glacier crossing and summit scramble on day 2 before hiking all the way out.

days.title: Approach to Sahale Glacier Camp
days.objective: Reach Sahale Glacier Camp
days.note: From the Cascade Pass Trailhead, switchback up to Cascade Pass (3.7 mi, ~1,800 ft), then continue up the Sahale Arm climbers' trail to the permitted camp at ~7,600 ft. The final 0.6-0.7 mi above the Arm is loose scree/talus on cairns with real exposure — go slow and watch weather.

days.title: Summit push and hike out
days.objective: Climb Sahale Mountain via the Sahale Glacier, then descend to the trailhead
days.note: An early start to cross the small, crevassed Sahale Glacier while snow is firm, then a short, exposed class 3-4 scramble and an awkward chimney move (about 5.0) to the 8,680 ft summit. Most parties return to camp, break it down, and hike all the way out to the car the same day rather than spend a second night.

camps_on_file.name: Sahale Glacier Camp

camps_on_file.name: Doubtful Lake
camps_on_file.notes: The lower fallback, roughly a mile and a thousand feet down a signed spur off the arm. days.note: Traverse from the col to the base of Cascade Peak's NW Chimney in the moat and climb the roughly 3-pitch route (loose crux crack, then a cleaner 5.8 chimney, then a short loose pitch and simul-climbing to the summit). days.title: Approach to Colonial Glacier basin camp

days.objective: Climb Colonial Glacier and the West Ridge to the summit, then descend all the way to the car
days.note: An alpine start gets the team across the glacier while it's still firm, up class 3 rock on the summit pyramid, and back to camp by midday. Most parties then break camp and hike all the way out the same day rather than adding a third night, making for a long but complete summit-and-out day.

camps_on_file.name: Colonial Basin bench camps, below the Pyramid-Colonial col
camps_on_file.notes: The standard first-night camp for Snowfield, Neve and Colonial, reached by a steep sustained climb from the Pyramid Lake trailhead with no easy water for much of it. trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day, roughly 25-mile round trip out of the Easy Pass Trailhead: backpack in to Cosho Camp, a long cross-country summit day (~4,400 ft of gain on loose gullies, snow, and class 3 rock), then hike back out.

days.title: Backpack in to Cosho Camp

days.note: Hike the Easy Pass Trail (3.6 mi, ~2,850 ft) to Easy Pass at 6,550 ft — snow often lingers on the pass into early July, so an ice axe is worth carrying. days.title: Summit day: Cosho Peak via south gullies
days.objective: Climb Cosho Peak (and optionally Kimtah) via the south gullies and upper east face
days.note: Alpine start with a light day pack. Follow the trail about a mile past camp, then leave it and climb one of the loose south-facing gullies (roughly 4,000 ft of gain, staying in the gully or on the rib to its west) to the 7,830 ft Kimtah-Cosho saddle. Grab the axe for the moderate snow slope on the north side up to ~8,1…

days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Easy Pass trailhead
days.note: Reverse day one: climb back up out of the Fisher Creek drainage to Easy Pass, then descend the Easy Pass Trail to the trailhead.

camps_on_file.name: Cosho Camp, Fisher Creek
camps_on_file.notes: This forested camp on the north side of Fisher Creek is the usual base for Cosho Peak and the eastern end of Ragged Ridge, reached over Easy Pass from the SR 20 trailhead and then down roughly 1,400 ft of switchbacks to the valley. It is an easy first day from the car, which is why parties use it despite the elevation …

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip (~16.2 mi, ~7,200 ft total gain) - the direct-start variant of the Southwest Buttress, slightly longer and more sustained than the standard line, with a full 11-13 hr summit day.

days.title: Approach to high camp near the McAllister/Marble Creek col

days.note: Same Eldorado Creek trail and glacier approach as the standard Southwest Buttress, camping within reach of the buttress's toe.

days.note: Climb the standard approach gully, then go straight up from its top where the standard line traverses right: two direct-start pitches (the 5.10a mantel crux, then 5.8+) rejoin the 1985 route at a large white slab. days.title: Hike out

camps_on_file.name: Marble Creek Campground, Cascade River Road
camps_on_file.notes: Roughly eight miles up the gravel Cascade River Road from Marblemount, this is the practical place to spend the night before if you cannot start walking the same day. Its value is logistical: the Wilderness Information Center wants your permit activated in person the day before, or before late morning on your start day…

trip_plan.totalNote: Climb steeply from the Eldorado trailhead to a ~7,400 ft camp, cross the Inspiration and McAllister Glaciers to climb the East Ridge and descend the Northwest Ridge, then hike out on day three.

days.title: Hike to the Eldorado high camp
days.objective: Set up high camp near 7,400 ft
days.note: Hike from the Cascade River Road trailhead, cross the creek, and climb steeply via the Eldorado Glacier to the East Ridge of Eldorado Peak, roughly 4 miles and 6,000 ft of gain. Set up camp around 7,400 ft and review gear and technique.

days.title: Climb Dorado Needle
days.objective: Climb the East Ridge and return to camp
days.note: Rope up and traverse the Inspiration Glacier onto the McAllister Glacier, then descend to the col at the base of Dorado Needle's East Ridge and climb it to the summit. Downclimb and rappel the Northwest Ridge back to the col, then retrace the glacier traverse to high camp.

days.title: Descend to the trailhead
days.objective: Return to the Eldorado trailhead
days.note: Descend to the trailhead, including the final creek crossing, typically finishing by early evening.

trip_plan.totalNote: A 3-day trip (~14 mi, ~6,400 ft total gain) but the shortest/easiest of Dorado Needle's ridge lines - only 3 pitches of easy 5th class - so summit day is typically a half-day, 6-8 hrs camp-to-camp, rather than a full push.

days.title: Approach to Inspiration/McAllister Glacier high camp
days.objective: Reach high camp below the Northwest Ridge
days.note: Same Eldorado Creek trail and glacier approach as the other Dorado Needle routes, to a high camp in the 7,000-7,500 ft range.

days.title: Climb the Northwest Ridge
days.objective: Summit via the Northwest Ridge and return to camp
days.note: Cross the Inspiration and McAllister Glaciers to gain the ridge, then follow easy 5th-class rock (only ~3 short pitches) along the crest to the summit - the shortest and easiest of Dorado Needle's ridge routes. days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Break camp and return to the trailhead
days.note: Reverse the approach back to the Cascade River Road trailhead.

days.title: Approach to high camp near the McAllister/Marble Creek col
days.objective: Reach high camp below the Southwest Buttress
days.note: Same Eldorado Creek trail approach, continuing over talus and the Eldorado Glacier toward the Inspiration/McAllister Glacier area, camping within striking distance of the snow gully below the Marble Creek-McAllister col that gives access to the buttress.

days.title: Climb the Southwest Buttress
days.objective: Summit via the Southwest Buttress and return to camp
days.note: Cross the glacier to the snow-filled gully below the col, gain the blocky toe of the buttress, then climb roughly 9 pitches of steep cracks, slabs, and photogenic gendarme traverses (5.7-5.8) to the summit.
